metadata.title: Why Web Search Never Runs Your Code but Your Own Tool Always Does — with Identical Syntax
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: why does web search finish inside one request while your own tool call always needs two, when both are declared the same way? Lands the carry-out that round-trip count is set by who can execute, not by how the tool is declared.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B04 (.webSearch/serverTools vs lookupFavorites/tools declaration case, paid off with the osmosis/checkNotes example plus both directions)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes a tool call always comes back through their own code. Wrong guess — sometimes it does, sometimes it doesn't. Why web search never runs your code, but your own tool always does.

beats.narration_text: Declaring a tool feels uniform — you list it, Claude can call it, so every call should behave the same way afterward. The natural guess: the model emits a call, your code runs it, you send the result back. That's true for your own tools. It is not true for web search.

shot.new_visual_element: A single 'declare a tool' card branching into two identical-looking call shapes; one keeps its emit-run-send loop, the other's loop breaks open

production_viz.label: Same declaration, different behavior
production_viz.mechanic: One 'DECLARE A TOOL' card at top branches into two identical call shapes below it, each a closed loop labelled EMIT → RUN → SEND BACK. The right-hand loop cracks open at RUN, in terracotta, with a small 'not true for web search' caption.

beats.narration_text: Here's the concrete case. `.webSearch(maxUses: 5)` sits in `serverTools`; a Swift function called `lookupFavorites()` sits in `tools` — same file, same declaration style. Web search runs on Anthropic's servers and its results land inside that same turn. `lookupFavorites` triggers a tool-use block that only your own app can act on.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- two declaration cards side by side, serverTools/.webSearch and tools/lookupFavorites(), one path closes on itself, the other exits to a labelled 'your app' box

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- serverTools vs. tools
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Left mono card: `serverTools: [.webSearch(maxUses: 5)]` labelled SERVER-SIDE. Right mono card: `tools: [lookupFavorites()]` labelled CLIENT-SIDE. From the left card a short arrow loops back to a CLAUDE label. From the right card an arrow exits to a box labelled YOUR APP, captioned 'only your app can run this'. THIS COMPOSITION RETURNS AT B04.

beats.narration_text: Round-trip count comes down to who can execute. Web search needs a live index and a sandbox — infrastructure Anthropic already runs, so it finishes the call itself, in that same turn. `lookupFavorites()` is arbitrary code on your device — only your app can run it, which forces the model to stop and wait for a second request.

shot.new_visual_element: Two lanes: ANTHROPIC'S SERVERS closing its own loop; YOUR DEVICE, its arrow exiting the frame and re-entering as a second request

production_viz.label: Who can execute
production_viz.mechanic: Left lane: ANTHROPIC'S SERVERS, with small index and sandbox icons, a single arrow looping back on itself labelled 'closes in-turn'. Right lane: YOUR DEVICE, an arrow that exits the frame's edge (terracotta) and re-enters lower down labelled 'second request'.

beats.narration_text: Say to Claude, "search osmosis, then check my notes." The search resolves inside that request — no callback into your code. `checkNotes()` can't: the model emits the call, your code runs it, and a second request carries the answer back. It doesn't matter how trivial your function is — even one line forces that round trip. And it doesn't matter how often web search fires — every call still resolves in-turn, because Anthropic still holds the execution.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- the osmosis search closes its own loop; checkNotes() exits and re-enters; both-directions captions

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- one boundary, tested both ways
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 COMPOSITION RETURNS: the SERVER-SIDE card's loop now carries the label 'search osmosis' and closes cleanly on CLAUDE. The CLIENT-SIDE card's arrow now carries 'checkNotes()', exits to YOUR APP, and a second arrow returns captioned 'answer back'. Beneath, two small captions: 'trivial function — still round-trips' under the client side, 'fires twice — still in-turn' under the server side.

beats.narration_text: It isn't the syntax that decides the round trip — it's who can execute. Anthropic runs its own tools inside the turn; only you can run yours, so the model has to stop and come back for the answer.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. In my Claude app, I have one tool declared as a server-side tool, like web search, and one declared as a client-side tool that calls my own code. Walk me through what happens at the network level for each — how many round-trips, who executes the tool, and where the result enters the conversation — so I can reason about latency budgets in my app. Liam, in for Bear.
